# @guowenzhang/dsh-mcp-manager
中文 | English
## The problem this plugin solves
Adding MCP servers to DeepSeek Harness is inconvenient, and loading every configured server's tools
by default consumes substantial context.
This plugin adds server creation, editing, and per-row switches to the settings page. With on-demand
loading, the initial context contains only MCP names and descriptions; the model enables servers as
needed during a session. Tool filtering lets you load only the tools you select.
In the plugin list, display names and descriptions follow the Harness language setting in English or
Chinese (English is the default fallback); English names use the package name without its npm scope
, Chinese names describe the purpose, and installation still uses the unchanged real package name.
## Screenshots
**MCP management: Servers**
**MCP management: Settings**
One page with two tabs: **Servers** holds the roster, **Settings** holds the loading mode and how mu
ch of a tool list one call hands to the model. The server list scrolls independently while the page
heading, tabs, Add button and filters stay in place. Agent preset names use the same Host translatio
ns as the new-session picker and update with the interface language; authored names remain unchanged
. The roster is one list — global rows first, labelled **Global**, then the rows of the agent preset
picked in the filter bar. Click the card itself to open the editor: **Config / Credentials / Tools*
*; a row that carries an environment or a header opens straight on **Credentials**. Where an added r
ow is written is chosen in the dialog's own **Config scope** select, which lists the global plane an
d every declared agent preset in one field; the tools pane shows each tool's estimated token cost an
d the totals for what is loaded and what a rule would drop. A switch that fails reports in its own r
what is loaded and what a rule would drop. A switch that fails reports in its own row with a retry.
## Install
Requires DeepSeek Harness, `pnpm`, and Node.js ≥22.18 or ≥24.2.
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart the host and refresh the page, then open **Settings → MCP management** to add servers and de
scribe their purpose. The page has two tabs: **Servers** (the roster: one list, global rows first wi
th a **Global** label, then the rows of the agent preset the filter bar selects; click a card to ope
n its editor, whose **Config / Credentials / Tools** panes hold the JSON, the environment or headers
, and the tool list) and **Settings** (**MCP loading**, where Dynamic insert is the default, followe
d by how much of a tool list reaches the model). The **Config scope** select picks an added row's ho
me in one field: the global plane, or one agent preset. In the add form the two fields marked `*` (s
erver name, JSON configuration) are required, and the server name is filled from the JSON you paste
(`npx -y @upstash/context7-mcp` → `context7`); once you edit it yourself, it is yours.
See AGENTS.md for other installation methods and development instructions.
## Reduce context further: search, paging, names only
**Settings → MCP management → Settings** controls how much of a tool list reaches the model, and car
ries the loading mode. The MCP specification has no query parameter on `tools/list` and no names-onl
y listing, and the client best-practices guide places progressive discovery in the host — which is w
he client best-practices guide places progressive discovery in the host — which is what this tab is:
| Setting | Effect |
| **Tool search** (`search`) | Registers `mcp_search`: the model finds tools by keyword across every

discovered server and gets names plus one-line descriptions only. |
| **Index uncached servers** (`
searchIndex`) | Lets a search connect to a server it has no tool list for (3 at a time, 8 seconds ea

ch). Off by default, so a search stays a cheap read. |
| **Items per listing** (`pageSize`) | `mcp_l

oad` / `mcp_search` list at most this many items and return `nextCursor` for the rest. |
| **Names a
nd descriptions only** (`namesOnly`) | `mcp_load` omits argument schemas by default; asking for one

tool by name still returns that tool's full schema. |
| **Tools collected per server** (`maxTools`)

| Caps the paginated `tools/list` walk, so an enormous server cannot flood a request. |
| **Show too
l annotations** (`annotations`) | Carries the server's `readOnlyHint` / `destructiveHint` / `idempot

entHint` / `openWorldHint` into listings. |
| **Hide destructive tools** (`hideDestructive`) | Keeps
tools whose `destructiveHint` is explicitly true out of the session entirely. |
The same page shows what the tool catalogue has cached (servers, tool counts, age) and can clear bot
h memory and disk records. Every switch is a live setting: it applies to the next load, search, or r
e-index without a restart.
[该节后续省略]
## Notes
- **On-demand loading covers both planes, and nothing starts at host start-up.** Under Dynamic inser
t (`dynamic`, default) and Lazy loading (`lazy`) an allowed row is suppressed before its plugin ever
runs, so host start-up and Agent preset rebuilds start no MCP process at all; the first `mcp_load`
starts the connection. Global composition rows follow the same loading mode: Load all (`eager`) moun
ts them from the composition, while `dynamic` / `lazy` keep them held until `mcp_load` starts one on

a connection shared with other sessions. Tool filters still do not take effect on a global row.
- *
*Load on demand, then reuse.** Connections live in a host-level pool keyed by row and connection con
figuration: the same server loaded again — by the same session, another session, or a subagent — reu
ses that one connection (for stdio, the same child process). `mcp_unload` releases only the calling
session's reference; the server stops when the last session releases it, and a session that ends rel
eases its references. The connection lives as long as the host process — committing a different load
ing mode rebuilds the tool set and releases that mode's references, and a host restart means loading

the server again. "Nothing starts at start-up" holds whether or not the server was loaded before.
